cards.explanation: The answer is that Paul came without eloquence or wisdom. He says, "…I did not come with eloquence or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God." No fancy speech and no polished words, friends. He still proclaimed the testimony about God, just without the polish.

The answer is nothing except Jesus Christ and Him crucified. Paul says, "…I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified." That was his resolve while he was with them. Jesus Christ, and Him crucified, is the focus he names.
The answer is True. Paul says, "I came to you in weakness and fear, and with much trembling." He doesn't dress it up, friends. It's an honest thing to say about yourself, and I respect it.

The answer is a demonstration of the Spirit's power. Paul says his message and preaching were "…not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power…" The power wasn't his, bakers. It came with the message from the Spirit.

The answer is False. Paul wanted their faith "…not rest on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power." That's why he came without polished speech. If the faith rested on his talking, it would be a lot to put on one man, friends. God's power can hold it.

The answer is False. Paul says it is "…not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing." The ones he says are coming to nothing are the rulers of this age. The wisdom he speaks is of a different kind, the wisdom of God (verse 7).
The answer is "before." God's wisdom was something "…He destined for our glory before time began." Paul puts the destining before time began, friends, and that's his timing, so I'll stick with it.

The answer is that they would not have crucified the Lord of glory. Paul says, "For if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory." The rulers of this age didn't understand God's wisdom. That's a heavy verse, so I'll just let it sit.

The answer is that God revealed it to us by the Spirit. Paul says no eye has seen, no ear has heard and no heart has imagined what God has prepared (verse 9). Then he says, "But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit." It's a gift, friends, and we get to open it.

The answer is his own spirit within him. Paul asks, "For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him?" Your thoughts stay in you unless you share them. Even my best ideas stay in here until I say them out loud.

The answer is so we may understand what God has freely given us. Paul says we received the Spirit who is from God "…that we may understand what God has freely given us." Freely given means a gift, friends. The Spirit helps us see what's been handed to us.

The answer is False. Paul says he speaks "…not in words taught us by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit…" He expresses "…spiritual truths in spiritual words." The Spirit gave the truth and the words to go with it, bakers.

The answer is foolishness to him. Paul says, "For they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned." The natural man doesn't accept them, and that's how they look to him. Understanding takes the Spirit, friends.

The answer is that the spiritual man judges all things. Paul says, "The spiritual man judges all things…" The spiritual man is the one who can discern spiritual things, which the natural man can't. That's quite a difference between those two, bakers.

The answer is True. Paul says, "The spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not subject to anyone’s judgment." Those are his words, and I'll leave them just as he wrote them, friends. That's verse 15.

The answer is the mind of Christ. Paul says, "But we have the mind of Christ." Nobody can instruct the Lord, yet we have the mind of Christ. That's a gift to be grateful for, friends, not something to brag about.
